best_for: Writers, researchers and docs teams on Windows who draft in Markdown and need clean Word, HTML, EPUB or PDF output with citations, from one command.

points.title: Converts between dozens of formats
points.text: Pandoc reads and writes Markdown, HTML, LaTeX, Word .docx, ODT, EPUB, reStructuredText, Org, Jupyter notebooks, Typst and many more. It can also turn Markdown into PowerPoint or reveal.js slides.

points.title: Citations done for you
points.text: Write a citation key in your text and pandoc builds formatted references and a bibliography from BibTeX, BibLaTeX or CSL data, in any of hundreds of CSL styles. Citations work in every output format.

points.title: PDF needs a second program
points.text: Pandoc does not make PDFs on its own. By default it uses LaTeX, and the project suggests MiKTeX on Windows; you can pick another engine such as wkhtmltopdf or WeasyPrint with --pdf-engine.

points.title: It is a command-line tool
points.text: There is no window to click through. You run commands like `pandoc -o out.docx in.md`, or call it from an editor or script that wraps it.

points.title: Expect some loss from rich formats
points.text: Pandoc keeps structure such as headings, lists and tables, but not layout details like margins. Converting from formats richer than its Markdown, such as complex Word tables, can lose detail.

points.title: Extend it with Lua filters
points.text: Lua filters and custom readers and writers let you reshape a document during conversion. The project's statically linked binaries cannot load Lua filters that depend on modules written in C.

points.title: Windows install options
points.text: The listing here has x64 MSI installers for one user or all users, plus a zip, and keeps 71 versions. Mac users can use Homebrew or the official .pkg; Linux users get a .deb or tarball from the project, or their distribution's package.
